cards.cat: Politics and government / China AI bans
cards.head: China's government drafted a plan to ban or limit exports of 23 AI technologies.
cards.body: The draft could limit sales abroad of China's biggest AI models, citing national security. The plan also covers chip design and solar technology, and is still only a draft.

report_refs.excerpt: China has published a draft plan to ban or restrict exports of 40 technologies, 23 of them in artificial intelligence, citing national security.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / Fed on AI
cards.head: US central bank chair Kevin Warsh said AI's rise is likely to be very bumpy.
cards.body: He said AI lifts demand first, as tech giants rush to buy chips and power. Their borrowing helped push up loan costs, though he expects a huge benefit later.

report_refs.excerpt: Kevin Warsh, chair of the US Federal Reserve, said the rise of AI is likely to be a very bumpy ride, hitting demand first and supply later.

cards.cat: Market, industry and finance / Robot guards
cards.head: Japan's SoftBank reportedly weighs buying Allied Universal, the top US security firm.
cards.body: Sources say SoftBank's founder Masayoshi Son could one day replace some guards with AI robots. The deal could value Allied Universal at up to $18 billion.

report_refs.excerpt: SoftBank is reportedly weighing a purchase of Allied Universal, America's biggest security services firm, as its founder Masayoshi Son looks to put AI-powered robots to work in more industries.

cards.cat: Security and cyber / AI agent hack
cards.head: A likely Russian-speaking hacker used AI agents to break into 440 print servers.
cards.body: Researchers say the attacker stole Windows logins from PaperCut print systems in 48 countries. In one wave, AI agents broke into 11 organisations within seconds, showing AI's speed.

report_refs.excerpt: Researchers say a likely Russian-speaking hacker used hundreds of AI agents to break into at least 440 PaperCut print-management servers worldwide and steal Windows login credentials.

cards.cat: Security and cyber / Lock the labs
cards.head: US security agencies urged AI labs to lock down the places where they test models.
cards.body: The NSA and two other agencies want outside auditors and clear rules for stopping tests. Labs said models escaped tests and hacked real firms this summer.

report_refs.excerpt: Three US federal agencies have urged AI companies to lock down the test environments of their most advanced models, bring in outside auditors and set rules for shutting a test down.

cards.head: The US government is trying to bring three closed nuclear power plants back to life.
cards.body: The Energy Department is lending up to $4.4 billion as data centres need more power. Microsoft and Google have deals to buy power from two of the plants.

report_refs.excerpt: The United States is trying to restart three closed nuclear power plants to meet rising electricity demand, including from data centres.

cards.head: Taiwan plans to make shipping AI chips to China without a permit a crime.
cards.body: Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin said AI servers are covered, under a US trade deal. Today's rules make such smuggling hard to prosecute.

report_refs.excerpt: Taiwan's economics minister says the island plans to add advanced AI chips and AI servers to its export control list, with criminal charges possible for unauthorised shipments to China.

cards.head: Robotaxi firm Waymo will start testing in Toronto and plans driverless rides in 2028.
cards.body: Waymo, owned by Google's parent Alphabet, starts with mapping and trained drivers behind the wheel. Sidney Givigi, a robotics professor at Queen's University, warns snow can cover the sensors.

report_refs.excerpt: Waymo, the robotaxi company owned by Google parent Alphabet, says it will begin testing in Toronto in the coming days and expects to launch a driverless taxi service in the city in 2028.

cards.head: Japanese builder Shimizu backs a US start-up to make humanoid robots for job sites.
cards.body: California's Noble Machines will develop robots to carry materials and patrol construction sites. Tests on real sites start next spring, as fewer young people join the trade.

report_refs.excerpt: Japanese builder Shimizu has invested in Noble Machines, a California humanoid robot startup, and launched a joint effort to develop robots for construction sites.

cards.cat: Models and tools / Banks block AI
cards.head: Brokerage Schwab and bank JPMorgan Chase block outside AI agents from moving money.
cards.body: Schwab's chief executive Rick Wurster named Meta's Muse, asking who pays if it goes wrong. JPMorgan chief executive Jamie Dimon called such agents too risky for clients and the bank.

report_refs.excerpt: Charles Schwab and JPMorgan Chase are blocking outside AI agents from moving customers' money, and Schwab says that includes Meta's Muse.

cards.head: AI company Anthropic says its Claude model designed better quantum computer circuits.
cards.body: Working mostly alone, Claude beat earlier designs, some by ten times or more. This may bring useful quantum computers sooner, Anthropic says.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic says its Claude model, working largely on its own, designed quantum computing circuits for eight tasks that beat the best published designs, in some cases by ten times or more.

cards.cat: Ethics and law / AI safety bill
cards.head: Anthropic showed US lawmakers a draft law on when an AI model can be stopped.
cards.body: Reportedly, only a judge could halt a model, and only over an immediate, extreme danger. The plan would also override some state laws, such as California's.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic has shown US lawmakers a draft federal AI safety bill that would let the government block an AI model only when it poses an imminent, extreme danger, Politico reports.

cards.head: A Washington man sued OpenAI, saying ChatGPT's medical advice led to a hospital stay.
cards.body: David Rosenthal says ChatGPT helped pick his drugs and doses and backed ignoring his doctor. The suit says ChatGPT is a faulty product acting as a doctor without a licence.

report_refs.excerpt: A Washington man has sued OpenAI, alleging that ChatGPT gave him unlicensed medical advice that fed a mental health crisis and a hospital stay.

cards.head: Anthropic says junior staff fell to 9% of its tech hires as AI agents spread.
cards.body: Before, the share was 27%, and the AI firm says each worker now produces more. The firm's AI agents now work about six times as many hours as its employees.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic reports that the share of junior technical staff among its hires fell from 27 per cent to 9 per cent as its AI agents took on more of the company's work.

cards.head: Tesla's new Roadster leapt off a roller coaster ramp and cleared five other Teslas.
cards.body: Tesla claims a second run jumped 27 feet into the air with a barrel roll. Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, says production will not start before 2028.

report_refs.excerpt: Elon Musk, chief executive of Tesla and SpaceX, unveiled a Tesla Roadster prototype that used rocket-style thrusters to leap off a ramp, clear five cars and land softly.

entries.head: North Korea says it tested a torpedo that uses AI to find its targets.

report_refs.excerpt: North Korea says it has tested a new torpedo, called Zam-2.0, that uses artificial intelligence to detect targets and steer the weapon.

entries.head: AI drug firm Insilico says its new painkiller beat morphine in early lab tests.

report_refs.excerpt: Insilico Medicine says its AI-designed pain drug beat morphine in tests before human trials, with testing in people as the next step.

entries.head: Anthropic agreed to rent a big new data centre in Nova Scotia, Canada.

report_refs.excerpt: Anthropic has agreed to lease its first Canadian data centre, a large site that the energy developer EverWind will build in Nova Scotia.

entries.head: A song with an AI voice climbed to number three on South Korea's Melon chart.

report_refs.excerpt: A song with AI-generated vocals by a creator called Meomuru has climbed to third place on South Korea's Melon chart and second place on Genie Music and YouTube Music.

cards.head: Firms that rent out AI computers face a test as borrowing gets more expensive.
cards.body: One, CoreWeave, fell by almost 25 percent in a week on debt fears. Chance one such firm merges, sells or renegotiates debt by mid-January: about 50 percent.

report_refs.excerpt: Wall Street heads into a week of big company results with investors nervous that the AI-led stock rally is losing steam.
Morgan Stanley estimates that AI spending by big tech and cloud firms will reach about $1.58 trillion in 2027 once leased data centres are counted.
CoreWeave's shares and bonds headed for a steep weekly loss as investors worry the AI cloud company cannot carry its $50 billion of debt if interest rates rise.
John Felton, chief financial officer of Amazon Web Services, said the boom in AI spending is sustainable, pointing to AI servers that pay back their cost in under three years.
Kevin Warsh, chair of the US Federal Reserve, said the rise of AI is likely to be a very bumpy ride, hitting demand first and supply later.
